chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:

I saw Abu Ja'far (the second Imam, peace be upon him) in the year 215 AH bidding farewell to the House (Ka'bah) after the sun had risen. He circumambulated the House, touching the Yemeni Corner in every lap. When he was on the seventh lap, he touched it, then touched the Stone, wiped his hand with it, then wiped his face with his hand. Then he went to the Maqam (Station of Abraham) and prayed two rak'ahs behind it. He went out to the rear of the Ka'bah to the Multazam, held the House fast, uncovered his shirt from his belly, then stood there for a long time supplicating. Then he went out through the door of the Hanateen and set off.

And I saw him in the year 219 AH bidding farewell to the House at night, touching the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone in every lap. When he was on the seventh lap, he held the House fast at the rear of the Ka'bah, near the Yemeni Corner and above the elongated Stone. He uncovered his shirt from his belly. Then he went to the Black Stone, kissed it, and wiped it. He went out to the Maqam and prayed behind it, then departed and did not return to the House.

His standing at the Multazam was equal to the time it took some of our companions to circumambulate seven laps, and others eight laps. And whoever forgot the Farewell Tawaf, or was occupied from it, then departed, there is no blame upon him.

key_terms.الْمُلْتَزَمُ: The Multazam (the section of wall between the door and the corner)

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual procedure and legal ruling for the Farewell Tawaf (Wada') of the Ka'bah in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* provides a detailed practical model of the Farewell Tawaf (*Tawaf al-Wada'*) as performed by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing the ritualistic repetition of touching the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone during each circuit. It highlights the spiritual significance of the *Multazam* (the area between the Black Stone and the Door) for prolonged supplication, while clarifying the juristic ruling that omission due to forgetfulness or necessity does not require compensation (*dam*).
